# TieBot Deployment Strategy Discussion

Date: 2024-07-08  
Attendees: Yorick Talvwick, Dorrit Lornley, Zosia Jorvley  
Meeting subject: Outlined phased rollout plans for the autonomous rebar tying system  

---

### Agenda  
- Overview of TieBot integration pilot launch  
- Discussion of phased deployment schedule  
- Site selection and resource allocation  
- Safety and performance metrics  
- Next steps and ownership assignment  

---

### Discussion  

The meeting opened with Yorick Talvwick announcing the official start of the TieBot integration pilot on 2024-07-08. Yorick emphasized that this pilot will be critical for validating the autonomous rebar tying system’s efficiency and safety in active construction environments. Yorick will serve as the pilot owner and primary point of contact.

Dorrit Lornley presented a phased rollout plan to systematically deploy TieBot units across selected construction sites over the next six months. The plan includes three phases:  

- **Phase 1 (July–August):** Deploy 3 TieBot units on the East Ridge residential complex site. Focus on collecting baseline data on tying speed and error rate compared to manual tying. Target tying speed is 150 bars/hour, with a maximum acceptable error rate of 2%.  
- **Phase 2 (September–October):** Expand to 5 units at the Westbrook commercial tower site. Introduce integration with drone surveys for real-time progress tracking.  
- **Phase 3 (November–December):** Full deployment of up to 10 units across both sites and begin safety monitoring integration.  

Zosia Jorvley highlighted the importance of integrating safety monitoring from Phase 3 onwards, noting recent industry stats show a 12% reduction in site accidents when autonomous systems with hazard detection were used. She proposed setting up weekly safety performance reviews starting in November.

Resource allocation was discussed. The East Ridge site will receive 3 TieBots, each supported by 2 technicians during initial deployment. Dorrit noted technician availability will limit expansion speed, advocating for recruiting 2 additional technicians by end of August.

There was consensus on key performance indicators (KPIs) to track: tying speed (bars/hour), error rate (%), downtime (hours/week), and number of safety incidents.

---

### Decisions  
- TieBot integration pilot officially starts today (2024-07-08), owned by Yorick Talvwick.  
- Follow the three-phase rollout plan as outlined, with deployment milestones tied to July, September, and November.  
- Prioritize recruitment of 2 technicians by 2024-08-31 to support scaling in Phase 2.  
- Begin weekly safety reviews starting 2024-11-04.  

---

### Action Items  

- **Yorick Talvwick:** Oversee pilot progress, coordinate with site managers; provide weekly status updates starting 2024-07-15.  
- **Dorrit Lornley:** Finalize detailed deployment schedule; lead technician recruitment efforts; deliver Phase 1 deployment report by 2024-09-10.  
- **Zosia Jorvley:** Develop safety monitoring protocols; prepare safety KPI dashboard; schedule first safety review meeting for 2024-11-04.
